paragraphs.topic: Web supports individual/multi-user tasks, request input, status, results, approvals and controls.
Workflow service owns work stages and human waits; TC reservation/status/authorization are server-mediated.
Temporal manages human waits, timers, failure recovery and resume after restart.
Temporal is chosen for long human waits/recovery; it does not guarantee exactly-once external side effects, which require deduplication and state inspection.
X02 prepares notes and release manifest; X03 human approval; after approval, substantive content changes require another review; P26 failure must not repeat release.
WAITING_HUMAN includes document submission, question, route confirmation, permission confirmation and release confirmation.
RECONCILING means an external result is uncertain and must be checked against actual process/device/remote state.
Infrastructure retry default is three total attempts with 10s/30s backoff; business rework is at most three cycles before human decision; project profile may tune limits.
Lost response during flash/push/PR/tag is not blindly retried; inspect journal/remote result, otherwise route to RECONCILING and a human.
Results carry job/step/cycle/attempt/execution identity; stale attempts remain historical and cannot unlock the current gate.
Role prompts specify allowed paths, but isolation must also use OS accounts, workspace and credential scope plus patch checks.
Flash profile explicitly lists partitions, slots, prerequisites and recovery procedure; AI cannot infer unlock/wipe/relock.
After PC restart or interrupted command, inspect current mode and use project recovery procedure or human task; do not promise automatic rollback.
API writes command and outbox atomically; dispatcher forwards command_id; workflow checks revision/state and deduplicates.
HTTP 202 means durable acceptance, not completion; retries deduplicate and stale revision/body conflicts.
Artifact metadata precedes bytes; size/hash validation precedes availability; downloads recheck authorization; displayed logs are secret-redacted.
Original route table includes plan decision, human submissions, controls, release manifest, approval and events beyond current G4 routes.
Human inbox covers assigned steps/questions/permissions/device work/retry limits; UI permits submission or retry.
Release approval binds a manifest digest containing commit, image, validation bundle, rule/profile versions, repository/target/mode/version and notes hash.
Publisher rechecks current manifest, approval, permission and remote target; changed target/rebase requires new candidate and validation/approval.
External publish is intent → execution → remote query → stored receipt; retry queries previous result first.
Each job has isolated workspace and build output; only one writer per workspace; worker and publisher accounts are separate.
Operational recovery backs up business DB, Temporal persistence, artifact volume and configuration versions together; RPO/RTO remain internal operational decisions.

data_and_state_contracts.anchor: Owner comes from authentication; attempts are immutable; plans/manifests immutable; artifact URI is not a browser-provided path; human task has one effective completion/version; approval is bound to manifest and stale/revoked approval is unusable; release action idempotency is by destination and key, unknown status requires reconciliation; Temporal is authoritative while PostgreSQL stores inbox/outbox/projections; 202 is not final success; command+outbox atomic; artifact hash/size verified before persistence; receipt before final state.

Skip/reuse requires evidence and is not PASS; failures start a new cycle; approvals bind to release digest; no same-workspace concurrent writers; old-cycle results never unlock current cycle; side effects are not blindly replayed; default retry ceilings appear at lines 434-449.

A failed step stays FAILED and retry creates a new attempt; pause records resume state/step; cancellation preserves already-published remote state and reconciles; aggregate state must retain active child-step detail.
Task includes workspace id and writable paths; one writer/workspace; role scope is reinforced by OS account/workspace/credential separation; agent completion is not a quality gate PASS.
Profile contains release mode/repository/target/version/reviewers and approval flags; example permits non-distinct approver; mock evidence cannot authorize real release.

code_and_schema.finding: Settings has mode, DB/OIDC/security settings and optional Node/profile store paths; no workspace root or workspace owner/mode policy setting exists.

create_app accepts filesystem but only assigns app.state.filesystem; JobService is constructed without it. Routes currently cover auth/session, job create/list/snapshot and command status only; there is no workspace reconciler startup or workspace route.

JobService has no filesystem dependency. Create inserts a workspace intent in the same transaction as job/command/outbox, relying on SQL defaults. Job Snapshot only returns pristine DRAFT plus empty steps and last_event_id; no workspace state is exposed.

workspace_intents already has job_id, command_id, DB-generated stable workspace_token, RESERVED/PROVISIONING/READY/ERROR, generation, claim_token, claim_expires_at and error_code, with FK to the accepted command. Runtime has SELECT and column-limited UPDATE for intent state/claim/error columns; operator can SELECT. Current schema does not record a filesystem path or marker digest.
Auth retention migration; no workspace table or filesystem policy change.

current_b02_state.search_result: The only current service references to filesystem are the create_app parameter and app.state assignment; there is no workspace/reconcile/marker implementation. Workspace references in the implementation are the atomic intent insert and SQL schema.

g5_should_deliver: A filesystem workspace isolated by server-created job UUID under one fixed trusted root; never derive a path from request/title/user/profile text and never accept a browser path.
Create and verify the contract's private directory layout with owner/mode checks and an identity marker bound to job_id and the already-persisted stable workspace_token.
A bounded multi-reconciler claim/fencing protocol and restart/idempotent recovery that never promotes READY before durable file and directory sync plus matching live claim.

Conservative error handling: symlink, mismatched identity/token, unexpected content, ownership/mode violations, filesystem failures and ambiguous residue remain visible as ERROR/manual investigation; unknown data is not recursively deleted or adopted.
Independent actual-filesystem and process-fault evidence for collision/race, crash boundaries, stale claims, permissions and recovery; retain pending accepted command/outbox and pristine DRAFT job.
must_stay_separate: B03 owns Temporal execution, outbox consumption, job/command transitions, agent/worker execution, workflow step records and actual single-writer worktree enforcement.
B04 owns connected web/SSE/event presentation and notification inbox; G5 must not claim that job/log/image/device HTTP isolation is fully accepted.
B09 owns device registration, lease and bridge behavior; B11 owns release manifests, digest approvals, publisher credentials and remote reconciliation.

AT-21 remains incomplete until job, logs, images, device, file-path and session isolation are all exercised through their actual endpoints/resources; a workspace-only G5 pass cannot mark the original case passed.

Operational storage-root approval, production owner/service account, filesystem/mount behavior, backup/restore, capacity, retention, RPO/RTO and production deployment remain environment acceptance, not synthetic local G5 proof.
original_policy_vs_g5_scope.approval_boundary: The original workflow's X01 path-plan decision and X03 release-manifest approval are workflow/human gates; the latter binds to the current manifest digest. Workspace reservation/provisioning is not an approval and must not turn an ordinary accepted CreateJob into release, profile-eligibility or publisher authority.

supplemental_contract_questions.question: What exact fixed workspace root is configured, how is it pre-provisioned/validated, and which service UID/GID, mount and root mode are trusted? Startup and every path operation need a symlink-safe boundary; no request field may choose it.
supplemental_contract_questions.why: Current Settings has no root field; existing plan says an existing root but does not identify configuration source or owner policy.

supplemental_contract_questions.question: Pin the exact relative layout and exact marker encoding/bytes/hash/mode, including safe create-once algorithm and no-follow descriptor-relative checks. Specify how READY paths are treated once B03 legitimately writes into source/tc/artifacts.
supplemental_contract_questions.why: Plan names source/tc/artifacts and a marker object, but exact serialization/publication operations and the boundary between allowed future outputs and corrupt unexpected contents need a testable oracle.

supplemental_contract_questions.question: Pin lease expiry clock, claim query/locking, generation/token increments, heartbeat or no-heartbeat model, expiry reclaim, and conditional final UPDATE. Define what a stale live reconciler may still do to disk and prove it cannot commit READY or overwrite/remove a valid workspace.
supplemental_contract_questions.why: SQL has generation/token/expiry columns, while current implementation has no claim algorithm; filesystem effects cannot be transactionally fenced by SQL alone.

supplemental_contract_questions.question: Define retry sources/transitions from ERROR or expired PROVISIONING, fixed error-code mapping, whether READY is revalidated, and what exact empty/matching-marker residue may be resumed. Specify when manual intervention is required.
supplemental_contract_questions.why: The intended state names and recovery principle exist, but retry transition eligibility and the rule for safely recognizing partially completed files are not pinned.

supplemental_contract_questions.question: Define injected filesystem operation semantics and hooks for mkdir/open-with-no-follow/write/fsync/close/link-or-equivalent/publish/directory-fsync/parent-fsync and process kill boundaries; specify expected behavior after each injected failure.
supplemental_contract_questions.why: Plan requires independent failures around mkdir, marker publication, sync and READY commit, but there is no implemented filesystem API or operation-level oracle.

supplemental_contract_questions.question: Define deterministic handling for ENOSPC, read/write/sync errors, excessive unexpected entries and path/marker size, while preserving unknown files and accepted DB state.
supplemental_contract_questions.why: Plan calls out insufficient space and no deletion/adoption but gives no bounded directory/marker resource limits or fixed error result.
